title: Christmas Market at Blackpool Cricket Club
summary: A festive afternoon of gifts, sweet treats and decorations from local small businesses at Blackpool Cricket Club on Sunday 15 November 2026. Free entry, raising money for Mind.

posters.alt: Poster for the Christmas Market at Blackpool Cricket Club on Sunday 15 November 2026, 1pm to 5pm, free entry

intro: Come along for a gorgeous festive afternoon at Blackpool Cricket Club, supporting small local businesses and getting a head start on your Christmas shopping.

sections.heading: What to expect
sections.html:
Plenty of stalls, with gifting, sweet treats, decorations and more. The stalls are fully sold out, so there will be a full line-up of traders to browse.

The bar will be open throughout the afternoon, and you could even book yourself a table for Sunday lunch while you are there.

sections.heading: Supporting a good cause
sections.html: The market is raising money for Mind, the mental health charity, so every visit helps.

title: Christmas Market at Christ King Church

posters.alt: Poster for the Christmas Market at Christ King Church, Saturday 21 November 2026, 11am to 3pm, free entry, listing some of the local businesses attending

intro: Lots of handmade gifts, unique finds and treats, with something for everyone. A great way to get a head start on your Christmas shopping while supporting local small businesses.

sections.heading: Who will be there
sections.html:
Stalls so far include Boo Blooms, Resin by Olivia, Bling by Amy, Inner Sparkle and The Dessert Lab, with more to be announced.

Mr Whippy Blackpool will be outside serving ice creams and waffles.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.html: Christ King Church is at 241 Bispham Road, Blackpool FY2 0LB. Entry is free, so just turn up on the day.

title: Mum's Playin' Out
summary: Free events for new mums in Layton: poetry, drag bingo, rag wreath making, baby-wearing dance and comedy, with babies welcome. Part of Pride in Place Layton.

posters.alt: Poster for Mum's Playin' Out, a series of free events for new mums in Layton, part of Pride in Place Layton

sessions.name: Playdate Poetry
sessions.blurb: Come and listen to some spoken word, then join other mums to explore what "playing out" looks and feels like postpartum. No experience needed. Babies 2 and under welcome.

sessions.name: Baby Friendly Drag Bingo
sessions.blurb: Daytime drag bingo for mums who miss feeling like themselves. Daft prizes, a fabulous drag queen and a proper laugh. Adult content, so babies 18 months and under welcome.

sessions.name: Rag Wreath Making
sessions.blurb: Not a baby craft, a loud and messy one for you. Make a bright rag wreath, have a chat and take it home. Wonky is the look. Babies 2 and under welcome.

sessions.name: Baby-Wearing Dance
sessions.blurb: Join Charlie from "Dance Like a Mother": baby in the carrier, music up, dancing like no one can see. Two left feet welcome. Babies from 8 weeks to 2 years.

sessions.name: Baby Friendly Comedy
sessions.blurb: Comedy clubs don't want your baby. We do. Daytime laughs with the fabulous comedians Black Liver and friends. No shushing. Adult content, so babies 18 months and under welcome.

venue.name: Argosy Community Centre, Layton Institute and The Grange

intro: Mum's Playin' Out is a run of free events for new mums in Layton, designed to support mental health, sense of identity and joy. Babies are welcome at every session.

sections.heading: About the series
sections.html:
Mum's Playin' Out is part of Pride in Place Layton. Each session is free and aimed at new mums who want to feel like themselves again, meet other mums, and have some fun, with the baby right there beside you.

Each session has its own age guidance for babies, so check the dates below to find the right one for you.

title: Barbie Spooky Styling Session
summary: A free children's Barbie and Ken styling and play session at Layton Library on Friday 30 October 2026, 10:30am to 12:30pm. Fancy dress optional. Booking essential.

intro: A free children's Barbie and Ken styling and play event at Layton Library, hosted by Vintagebarbieclare. Fancy dress is optional and everything you need is provided.

sections.heading: What happens

Children pick their Barbie or Ken, choose an outfit and accessories, then either take photos (optional) or just play. Everything is provided.

title: The Deadbeats: Halloween Party Night

intro: Celebrate Halloween in style as The Deadbeats return to Layton Institute for a night of live music, dancing and entertainment.

sections.heading: The night
sections.html: Known for their energetic performances and crowd-pleasing setlists, The Deadbeats play a mix of rock, pop and party classics from across the decades. Whether you come for the music, the atmosphere or just a good night out, it is a great way to spend Halloween.

sections.heading: Fancy dress
sections.html: Fancy dress is completely optional, but why not get into the spirit? From witches and vampires to zombies and superheroes, everyone is welcome, and there may be a few surprises on the night.

sections.heading: Tickets

intro: An unforgettable night of live music as the P!NK tribute Beautiful Trauma, featuring Stacy Green as P!NK and a full live band, comes to Layton Institute.

sections.heading: The show
sections.html:
A high-energy show celebrating the biggest hits from one of the world's most iconic pop-rock stars. Expect powerhouse vocals, stunning stage presence and all the chart-topping favourites, including Just Like a Pill, Raise Your Glass, So What, Try, Who Knew, Get the Party Started, What About Us and many more.

Whether you are a lifelong P!NK fan or simply love a great live performance, it is packed with energy, singalong anthems and a fantastic atmosphere from start to finish.

sections.heading: Make a night of it
sections.html: Bring your friends, grab a drink from the bar and get ready to sing, dance and party the night away.

sections.heading: Tickets
sections.html: Tickets are £12 in advance or £16 on the door. They are expected to sell quickly, so book early to avoid missing out.

title: Elf Jr. The Musical
summary: AVR present Elf Jr. The Musical at Layton Institute on Sunday 20 and Monday 21 December 2026, 7pm. A festive family show full of songs, dance and Christmas magic.

posters.alt: Poster for AVR presents Elf Jr. The Musical, Sunday 20th December, 7pm, with a green elf boot in a snowy festive scene
Poster for AVR presents Elf Jr. The Musical, Monday 21st December, 7pm, with a green elf boot in a snowy festive scene

intro: Get ready to spread some Christmas cheer with AVR's magical production of Elf Jr. The Musical, a festive family adventure packed with laughter, singing, dancing and plenty of Christmas magic.

sections.heading: The story
sections.html: Based on the much-loved Christmas film, Elf Jr. The Musical tells the hilarious and heartwarming story of Buddy, a young orphan who mistakenly crawls into Santa's sack and is transported to the North Pole. Raised as an elf, Buddy soon discovers he is actually human and sets off on an unforgettable journey to New York City to find his real father and discover where he truly belongs.

sections.heading: The show
sections.html: With catchy songs, fantastic dance routines, colourful characters and lots of festive fun, the talented AVR performers are ready to bring this Christmas favourite to life on stage. Bring the whole family and get into the Christmas spirit.

sections.heading: Tickets
sections.html: There are two performances, on Sunday 20 and Monday 21 December, both at 7pm. Standard tickets are £12 and concession tickets (over 60 and under 16) are £10. Book early, as tickets are likely to go quickly.

intro: Help welcome the field creatures to the land, with an evening of unexpected light from artists AndNow.

sections.heading: The story
sections.html: Artist Ivan Morison worked in the field to turn the harvested crop into a series of sculptures, coated in sand and lime. They are creatures that will look after the meadow over winter.

sections.heading: The evening
sections.html: This Lightpool, come and help welcome these field creatures to the land, with an evening of unexpected light from artists AndNow. It runs from 6:30pm to 8pm at the Field of Dreams and is free.
